correctness.rationale: For every n≥2 the central hub has no, one or exactly two central arcs of opposing incidence; same-petal central two-arc fibers have an S^(n−2) external-petal join, other nonempty central fibers are cones. The stated fiberwise lexicographic matching leaves one vertex, one (n−1)-cell, and 2n n-cells; monotone central-set/lexicographic arguments establish acyclicity for all n. Integral join cycles consisting of each oriented triangle-boundary circle and S0 choices on all other petals evaluate with coefficient ±1 at a unique critical noncoface top simplex, hence give 2n independent n-homology classes; the cellular boundary is zero, and maps S^(n−1)→S^(n−1) of degree zero are null. Independent direct face and mod-two ranks for n=1,2,3 give n1 reduced H0=1,H1=2, n2 H1=1,H2=4, n3 H2=1,H3=6; these finite checks supplement the uniform proof and cannot replace it. The n1 exception is two disjoint circles.
